title: Affine weakly contractible hypercovers of qcqs pro-etale objects
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with small pro-etale site and universes [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] [def-weil-size-convention], and let $W\to X$ be a site object whose scheme $W$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. There exists an augmented simplicial object [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object] $U_\bullet\to W$ in this site, with each $U_p$ affine and weakly contractible, which is a hypercover of $W$. Here weakly contractible means that evaluation $F\mapsto F(U_p)$ on sheaves of sets on the full site $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ sends every epimorphism to a surjection. Hypercover means that for every $p\geq0$ the map $h_{U_p}\to M_p$ to its matching sheaf is an epimorphism. The matching sheaf in degree zero is $h_W$; in degree $p>0$ it is the finite limit of the compatible proper-face diagram in the category of sheaves of sets over $h_W$. In particular $M_1=h_{U_0}\times_{h_W}h_{U_0}$. The face and degeneracy maps satisfy the simplicial identities and commute with the augmentation. Representable sheaves here are the sheaves $h_V=\operatorname{Hom}_X(-,V)$.

proof.text: Work in the qcqs subsite $\mathcal D$ of $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ from [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-qcqs-finite-family-geometry]. The given $W$ belongs to it. Its fibre products and slice matching limits agree with scheme limits in the full site, its coverings are finite pro-etale coverings, and adjoining finitely many arrows preserves a covering. Let $\mathcal B$ consist of the affine objects of $\mathcal D$ that are weakly contractible for sheaves on the full site. For each $T\in\mathcal D$, [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-qc-affine-contractible-cover] gives a one-member cover $V\to T$ with $V$ affine and weakly contractible. Affine schemes are qcqs, so $V\in\mathcal B$. Thus the finite-cover and enlargement hypotheses of the finite-basis construction hold, with no affine hypothesis on $W$ or $X$.

source.place: Tag 09A1, proof of (2), qcqs subsite and choice of B; Tag 0F4P

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-finite-basis-hypercover-existence] to $(\mathcal D,\mathcal B,W)$. Obtain a genuine simplicial family hypercover $K_n=\{V_{n,i}\to W\}_{i\in I_n}$, with $I_n$ finite and all $V_{n,i}$ affine and weakly contractible in the full site. Regard these same families and component maps in the full site. By [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-qcqs-finite-family-geometry], the fibre products and finite limits in the slices agree, so their proper-face matching objects and arrows are the same. Each componentwise matching cover in $\mathcal D$ is a pro-etale cover in the full site. Thus $K$ is a family hypercover there as well; the face and degeneracy identities are equalities of the same scheme maps.

source.place: Tag 09A1, proof of (2), application of Tag 094K; transfer of matching coverings along the qcqs inclusion (Tag 0DAZ)

proof.text: Set $U_n=\coprod_{i\in I_n}V_{n,i}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-qcqs-finite-family-geometry], these finite disjoint unions lie in the site, are affine, and $\coprod_i h_{V_{n,i}}\cong h_{U_n}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-hypercover-disjoint-union] to the full-site family hypercover of step 2. On a component $V_{n,i}$ a simplicial operator with family data $(\alpha,f_i)$ is the composite of $f_i:V_{n,i}\to V_{m,\alpha(i)}$ and the corresponding coproduct injection into $U_m$. Composition and identity agree componentwise, hence agree on $U_n$ by its coproduct universal property. This supplies the augmentation and all simplicial identities. The cited disjoint-union theorem gives an epimorphism $h_{U_n}\to M_n$ for every degree, with matching limits explicitly over $h_W$, including $M_0=h_W$.

source.place: Tag 09A1, final sentences of proof (2); hypercovering.tex Tags 0DB1, 0DB2

proof.text: For an epimorphism $F\to G$ of sheaves of sets on the full site, [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-qcqs-finite-family-geometry] identifies its evaluation on $U_n$ with $\prod_i F(V_{n,i})\to\prod_i G(V_{n,i})$. Given a tuple of sections on the right, weak contractibility of each $V_{n,i}$ supplies a preimage in each of the finitely many factors. The tuple of these preimages gives a section of $F(U_n)$ mapping to the prescribed section. For the empty family both products are singletons. Therefore $U_n$ is weakly contractible in exactly the sense asserted. Together with step 3 this proves all clauses.
